title: Why Stores Doubled Shopping Cart Sizes

vo.en: Stop grabbing that giant shopping cart.

visual.description: First-person point-of-view shot rolling a metal grocery cart quickly down a modern supermarket aisle.

vo.en: Supermarkets doubled the size of carts, and researchers proved people immediately bought forty percent more.

visual.description: Close-up of a man's hands dropping multiple packaged food items into an oversized metal cart.

vo.en: Your visual cortex equates empty space with scarcity, triggering an urge to keep piling items inside.

visual.description: Top-down overhead view of a nearly empty wire shopping cart emphasizing vast vacant metal space.

vo.en: But here is the creepy part: even when you know this, that massive grid tricks your brain into feeling underprepared.

visual.description: Close-up of a man looking stressed while inspecting a long printed receipt under bright store lights.

vo.en: Carrying a hand basket forces physical awareness of weight, cutting impulse purchases instantly.

visual.description: A man's hand gripping a handheld plastic shopping basket while walking through fresh grocery produce.

vo.en: Subscribe to outsmart subconscious traps, and comment cart or basket below! Save your money next trip, which is why you must...

visual.description: Macro shot of a payment card tapping onto a point-of-sale terminal at a supermarket counter.
